The story primarily focuses on two characters—the narrator and Toby—both of whom are richly developed as complex, round characters. Initially, they present themselves through the flat lens of their professions and temporary statuses ("two people on contracts," a pragmatic marine biologist with a clipboard, and an observant choreographer accustomed to temporary rooms). However, as the rising tide forces them to confront the end of their residency, both characters show emotional depth, vulnerability, and evolution. Toby's mistake with the tide chart—a direct contradiction of his meticulous nature—reveals his distraction and deep affection for the narrator, while the narrator drops her detached, professional guard to admit she wants something permanent in Boston. The only other characters mentioned (the maintenance man and the marine station volunteer) are kept entirely off-screen and are given just enough quirky detail to ground the setting without feeling like hollow plot devices.
